before: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust active-cruise following distance and related frequently used driver-assistance settings while driving without searching through nested screen menus or taking attention away from the road.
after: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust active-cruise following distance, and other validated high-frequency driver-assistance settings, while driving through clear, low-attention access paths that avoid nested menu searching and minimize eyes-off-road time.
rationale: Keeps the customer value and solution neutrality, but narrows the broader driver-assistance claim to settings that are validated and replaces the absolute "without taking attention away" with a more credible low-attention/minimized-distraction standard.

before: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust everyday climate, radio/audio and navigation-display details during a trip through clear, predictable access paths that do not require digging through menu screens.
after: Customers shall be able to adjust high-frequency climate, audio and navigation-view tasks during a trip through clear, predictable access paths that avoid unnecessary menu searching and minimize driver distraction.
rationale: The revised statement remains customer-facing and solution-neutral while avoiding the over-specific US/EU/China evidence claim until EU and China pain-point validation is available.

before: Customers in the US, EU and China who drive electrified 5 Series variants shall be able to view and change everyday charging preferences without searching across multiple in-car menus.
after: Electrified 5 Series customers shall be able to view and change common charging preferences through a clear, consolidated in-car access path.
rationale: This is shorter, more customer-facing and avoids the stronger unsupported claim about customers currently searching across multiple menus, while preserving the intended usability outcome.
